battle.name: 第二次進攻燕國
battle.brief: 前222年，秦王政乘楚亡之後遣王翦、蒙武掃清燕國殘部。燕王喜前226年降秦卻退保遼東，秦恐其為北方患，遂大軍北進。遼東地寒，薊至襄平近六百公里，轉輸艱難；秦軍以弩陣壓制燕騎，卒擒燕王喜，燕國遂亡，同年置郡。卡面月牙劍的弧刃砍擊傳統，與此役秦軍的弩、戈、劍是並存的兩條冷兵器路線。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 前222年開戰時，交戰形勢已同十幾年前大不相同。關中一方是秦王政的秦國：韓、趙、魏三國已滅，趙王遷被遷於房陵，楚雖在前223年才被王翦主力擊滅，其殘部尚在江南；北方則只剩燕國的一支殘軍未經清剿。秦國的軍隊已從諸侯國的臨時徵發，轉為王權直轄的郡縣兵員與民夫混合體制，兵器由官營工坊統一供應，軍法嚴苛而賞罰有信。河北與遼河一線則是燕國的殘部：燕都薊在公元前226年被秦軍攻破，燕王喜奉獻土地求和，卻帶著少數人退到遼東，倚靠當地高寒的山野、戎狄部眾與匈奴勢力與秦軍周旋。秦王政不能容忍這樣一個政權存在，因為它正卡在秦的背後，又直對著草原。雙方在行政組織、兵源與後勤上的差距，是這場戰役真正的底色，也是燕國再無反擊餘地的根本原因。秦在關中與舊韓、趙、魏之地推行郡縣、徵發丁壯，靠的是一整套國家機器；燕則只剩王庭與近侍，能倚仗的兵源多為遼東本地部眾與歸附的邊民，指揮更近於部族聯盟。一邊是書同文、律同式的中央調度，一邊是倉促拼湊的臨時軍，這就決定了戰役的結局與規模。
countriesEn: When the war opened in 222 BC the strategic picture was nothing like it had been a decade earlier. On the Guanzhong side stood the state of Qin under King Zheng: Han, Zhao and Wei had already been destroyed, the former king of Zhao had been exiled to Fangling, and Chu, though it had only just been crushed by Wang Jian in 223 BC, still held out in the south-east. What remained of Yan in the north was a single retreating force. The Yan capital at Ji had fallen to the Qin army in 226 BC and King Xi of Yan had ceded territory and sued for peace, but he withdrew with a small following into Liaodong, where he relied on the harsh uplands, the Rong and Di settlements and the neighbouring Xiongnu to keep the Qin army at bay. King Zheng could not tolerate such a state existing, because it sat directly behind Qin and faced the steppe. The real balance of this campaign lay in the gap between the two sides in administration, manpower and logistics, and that gap is why Yan had no room left for a counter-stroke. In the Guanzhong homeland and the former lands of Han, Zhao and Wei, Qin worked through commanderies, levied peasants and ran a single state machine; Yan had nothing left but a court, its attendants, and soldiers drawn from the local Liaodong communities and the border folk who had attached themselves to the king, commanded less like an army than like a tribal confederation. On one side stood officials, a common script and a common standard of law; on the other, an improvised force patched together in haste. That difference decided the scale and the outcome of the campaign.
people: 秦方主事者是生於公元前259年、此時年近四十的秦王政，以及秦軍主帥王翦。王翦是滅六國過程中最能打的大將，前224至前223年以六十萬大軍滅楚，前222年又與蒙武同帥，掃取荊南、威脅越地。他作戰的特點是不求奇險：先看糧道是否撐得住，糧不足就退，糧足再攻，寧可多帶兵、多用時間，也不讓前線斷炊。副手蒙武出身北方邊防世家蒙氏，是蒙恬之兄。燕方是燕王喜，廟號烈王，公元前226年以降秦保國，前222年退保遼東，最終死在那裡；他的太子丹年輕時曾質於秦國，公元前227年遣荊軻刺秦，事敗之後下落不明，傳說最後亡命朝鮮半島。燕國大將劇辛於公元前251年在衍水一帶擊破秦軍，是燕軍最後一次成規模的野戰勝利，但此後燕廷再無可倚仗的大將，前線與中樞的意志從此再也合不攏來。王翦用兵的另一面是善待士卒：軍中糧食不足時他寧可退兵等待，也不許士卒以戰養戰，賞罰出於私門。蒙武久在北方，熟稔塞外氣候與騎射，一同北上追擊遼東殘部，正補上秦軍在塞外行軍的一課。燕王喜其人並無死戰之膽，前226年獻地求和已是他的底線，退保遼東不過是留一處退路；太子丹若在，尚可號召死士，如今只剩一位倦於戰事的國君與一批不肯降的邊地部眾。
peopleEn: On the Qin side the men in charge were King Zheng of Qin, born in 259 BC and now approaching forty, and the commander Wang Jian. Wang Jian was the most formidable of the generals who destroyed the six states: he took Chu in 224-223 BC with an army of six hundred thousand, and in 222 BC he and Meng Wu again led the operations that seized the lands south of the Jing river and brought pressure to bear on Yue. His method was the opposite of gambling. He measured the grain route first, withdrew whenever supply fell short, and attacked again only when the commissariat was full, preferring more men and more time to any risk of a hungry army on the line. His deputy Meng Wu came from the Meng clan, a family of long service on the northern frontier, and was the elder brother of Meng Tian. On the Yan side was King Xi of Yan, posthumously King Lie of Yan, who had surrendered in 226 BC to save his state and who died in 222 BC in Liaodong. His heir, the crown prince Dan, had been held as a hostage at the Qin court as a boy; in 227 BC he sent Jing Ke to try to kill the king of Qin, and after the attempt collapsed his whereabouts became unknown, with later tradition placing his end in the Korean peninsula. Yan's general Ju Xin had beaten a Qin army at the Yan river in 251 BC, the last substantial Yan field victory, but from then on the Yan court had no commander left to depend on, and the line and the court never again acted from a single will. Wang Jian's other characteristic was his care for the men: when grain ran short he would rather withdraw and wait than let the army live off the country, and rewards and punishments came from his own hand rather than through favourites. Meng Wu had served on the northern frontier for years and knew the steppe climate and the mounted bowman, which was exactly what was needed when the army went north after Liaodong. King Xi of Yan was not a man with a stomach for war: surrendering territory in 226 BC had already been his limit, and falling back into Liaodong was no more than a place to put the rear. With the crown prince gone there was no one left to call up die-hards, only an exhausted king and a body of border folk who would not kneel.
kits: 這一役真正在燕秦前線上出現的兵器，是秦軍的弩、戈、劍與甲胄。弩是秦軍壓制燕騎與城頭射手的骨幹：銅製的弩機裝在木臂之上，靠射手臂力張弦，戰陣中再以蹶張機或跪姿射手補足火力；有效射程一般認為在二百米上下，遠超常見弓矢，箭鏃作三棱形，專為穿透皮甲而製。步卒以戈為主兵，戈援向前彎出，勾啄與斬擊並用；秦劍則是直刃、柳葉形、菱形格、圓首，長約七十至九十公分，專為刺擊設計，劍脊上還有錯金銘文。防護上，秦墓出土的大量鐵札甲與鎧，說明秦國已能成批生產鐵甲，皮革包木的盾則是步兵常備。車兵仍在，但只作運載與衝陣之用，攻薊城時用雲梯，城下以長兵壓制守軍。卡面那把埃及月牙劍，正是同一時代另一端的答案：外彎單刃、刃背內凹、前段加厚，砍進去不必拔劍。燕軍手中與它功能相當的，是鉞與大斧一類砍劈兵器；秦軍手中同源而不同路的是戈。弧刃砍擊與直刃刺擊，是前二千年末歐亞東西兩端各自的選擇。除弩與戈劍外，秦軍仍用弓作騎兵與遠程機動的補充，戰車多由牛拉挽以載重，一車可載數日之糧；燕軍則以劫掠與游騎消耗秦軍的輜重。近年出土的秦墓材料中，弩機、銅箭鏃與鐵劍成組出現，說明弩與劍都已列為軍需品目，由官營工坊按規格供應。
kitsEn: The weapons actually present on the Yan-Qin front were the crossbow, the ge dagger-axe, the sword and the armour of the Qin army. The crossbow was the backbone of Qin firepower against Yan cavalry and against defenders on the walls: a bronze trigger mechanism was mounted on a wooden stock, the bow was drawn by the shooter's own strength, and draw-levers or kneeling shooters kept the line fed. Its effective range is generally put at around two hundred metres, several times that of an ordinary bow, and its bolts carried trilobate heads designed to punch through leather armour. Infantry fought primarily with the ge, whose curved blade served both to hook and to cut, while the Qin sword was a straight, double-edged, willow-leaf blade with a lozenge-shaped guard and a disc pommel, seventy to ninety centimetres long, designed for the thrust, with gold-inlaid inscriptions down the spine. For protection, Qin tombs have yielded large numbers of iron lamellar plates and armour, showing that the state could mass-produce iron body armour, and the common infantry shield was a wooden core faced with leather. Chariots survived, but were used for transport and for shock action; the siege of Ji was conducted with scaling ladders, and the work at the walls was done by troops with long weapons. The Egyptian khopesh on this card is the answer given at the other end of the same era: an outwardly curved single edge with a concave back and a thickened tip, which could be buried in a body and pulled out without effort. The closest functional counterparts in Yan's hands were the yue battle-axe and the heavy axe; the ge in Qin hands belonged to the same family of idea. Curved-blade cutting and straight-blade thrusting were the two separate answers the eastern and western ends of Eurasia had arrived at by the close of the second millennium BC. Besides the crossbow, the ge and the sword, the Qin army still used the bow for its cavalry and for long-range movement, and wagons were still largely ox-drawn, a single cart able to carry several days of rations; Yan answered with the same weapons, raiding the Qin baggage to starve the pursuers. In excavated Qin tombs the bronze crossbow triggers and arrowheads and the iron swords are found in sets, showing that crossbows and swords had become listed items of army supply, issued from state workshops to a common pattern.
tactics: 秦軍的部署分兩條線：主力仍由王翦、蒙武指向荊南，越地與楚地餘部在同年被壓平；另一支軍隊沿燕地北上，追入遼東。追擊戰最考驗的不是陣法，而是糧草與體力。薊至遼東襄平一帶直線距離接近六百公里，路上多山地與林莽，冬季嚴寒，車隊沿線屯糧、駝馬載食、步卒就糧而行，轉輸的損耗極大。作戰上，秦軍仍以前列弩手齊射壓制燕國騎兵與游擊隊，再以持盾持戈的步卒結陣推進，銳士以重裝步兵的身分作先鋒，負責破陣與追亡。燕軍的戰法是拖延與遊擊：不與秦軍正面硬拼，據城待援，利用熟悉的地形與游騎不斷襲擾秦軍的糧隊與後隊，消耗其時間與存糧。燕廷缺乏統一指揮，太子丹死後群龍無首，燕王喜只想割地求和，前線與中樞各行其是，遼東最終不是敗在一場決戰，而是敗在再也沒有可等之物。沿途秦軍設亭障、置烽燧以護糧道，遇燕騎則以車陣結圜、弩手居中而外環戈盾，迫其不能逼近；燕軍則利用遼河渡口與山地村落夜襲秦軍宿營，並派輕騎截斷糧車。燕國舊有的邊塞體系在秦軍到來時已多已廢弛，烽燧失修，訊息不通，遂使前線與薊城之間的消息斷絕。
tacticsEn: Qin split its effort across two lines. The main army under Wang Jian and Meng Wu still faced south-east, taking the lands south of the Jing and squeezing Yue, while a second force moved north along the old Yan territories in pursuit. In a pursuit the test is not formation but supply and stamina. The direct distance from Ji to Xiangping in Liaodong is close to six hundred kilometres, the route runs through uplands and woodland under a severe winter, grain was parked along the line, pack animals carried provisions and foot soldiers moved on their rations, so the losses in transport were severe. In contact, the Qin line still opened with a rank of crossbowmen massed against Yan horse and raiding parties, then advanced with shield-bearing ge infantry in close order, while armoured elite infantry served as the spearhead, breaking formations and running down fugitives. Yan answered with delay and harassment: no general engagement, fortified towns held in the hope of relief, and light horse sent to chew at Qin supply columns and rear echelons in country they knew. Yan command was divided and had no common will; after the death of the crown prince there was nobody to give the line one purpose, and King Xi preferred a negotiated cession to any further risk. Liaodong did not fall in a single decisive battle. It fell when there was nothing left to wait for. On the way north the Qin army established barriers and beacon towers to guard the grain road, and when Yan horse came up it closed into a wagon circle with the crossbowmen inside and the ge and shield on the outer ring, so that the raiders could not close; Yan in turn used the crossings of the Liao river and the mountain villages to strike at the Qin camp by night and sent light horse to cut the supply carts. The old Yan frontier system had already fallen out of repair by the time the Qin army arrived, its beacon towers unrepaired and its signals broken, and the line was therefore cut off from Ji entirely.
data: 有根據的數字大致如下：秦滅六國的次序為韓前230年、趙前228年、魏前225年、楚前223年、燕前222年、齊前221年，也就是說燕國是倒數第二個被併入的國家。燕國故地分置九郡，其中可確指的有廣陽、上谷、漁陽、右北平、遼西、遼東與薊等郡；秦統一之後在全國推行三十六郡的編制。兵員方面，記載最確切的一次大動員是王翦滅楚時的六十萬眾，這支部隊在楚亡之後即轉用於北方，而不是另造新軍。距離上，薊到遼東襄平直線接近六百公里，陸路更遠，車隊一日行程常以數十里計，因此遼東之役拖了數月而非數日。兵器尺寸上，戰國晚期秦劍通長約七十至九十公分，弩的常見有效射程一般估在二百米上下。規模的另一個側面是時間：前222年同年取荊南、降越，前221年齊不戰而降，七年之間秦由逐一兼併走到天下統一。出土的秦軍弩機與銅箭鏃多成組出現，反映弩已按批次配發；秦劍多有錯金銘文記作坊與年分，是兵器製造被納入國家管理的直接證據。就疆域而言，舊燕之地約當今日河北北部與遼西、遼東一帶，其九郡的設置範圍與後來漢代燕國諸郡幾乎重疊，說明郡界多有沿襲。
dataEn: The figures that can be relied on run as follows. Qin destroyed the six states in this order: Han in 230 BC, Zhao in 228, Wei in 225, Chu in 223, Yan in 222 and Qi in 221, which makes Yan the second to last state to be absorbed. The old lands of Yan were divided into nine commanderies, of which those that can be named with certainty include Guangyang, Shanggu, Yuyang, Youbeiping, Liaoxi, Liaodong and Ji; after unification Qin organised the whole realm into thirty-six commanderies. On manpower, the best attested mass mobilisation is the six hundred thousand men that Wang Jian took against Chu, and that same force was turned to the north once Chu had fallen rather than replaced by a new levy. On distance, the straight line from Ji to Xiangping in Liaodong is close to six hundred kilometres and the land route is longer; wagon convoys measured their daily progress in tens of li, so the Liaodong campaign took months rather than days. On weapons, Qin swords of the late Warring States period run from about seventy to ninety centimetres in length, and the effective range of the crossbow is generally estimated at around two hundred metres. A second measure of scale is the calendar itself: the lands south of the Jing and the submission of Yue fell in 222 BC, Qi surrendered without a battle in 221, and within seven years Qin had gone from annexing one state at a time to ruling the whole realm. The bronze crossbow triggers and arrowheads recovered from Qin tombs tend to appear in sets, which shows the crossbow was being issued in batches, and many Qin swords carry gold-inlaid inscriptions naming the workshop and the year, direct evidence that arms manufacture had been brought under state control. As to territory, the old lands of Yan covered roughly the northern part of present-day Hebei together with western and eastern Liaoning, and the nine commanderies set up there overlap almost exactly with the commanderies of the Yan state in Han times, which shows how much of the administrative boundary was inherited.
cause: 燕國之所以還能被秦追到遼東，是因為秦滅六國的次序裡燕排在最後。前227年秦使龐煖攻燕，燕遣荊軻刺秦於咸陽，事敗之後秦得以名正言順地反攻；前226年秦軍入薊，燕王喜獻地求和，秦置郡而去，但燕王喜並未真正北降，而是帶人保聚遼東，與當地戎狄及匈奴往來。對秦王政而言，這是一根必須拔掉的刺：燕國扼守北方的關隘與要道，只要它還在，秦就不能放心把兵力與注意力投向南方與東南；前223年楚亡之後，北方只剩這一處尾巴，集中大軍收拾遼東，遂成統一戰役的最後一步。從燕的方面看，前222年並沒有再出現新的刺秦行動，開戰純粹來自秦的兼併意圖，以及燕王喜遲疑不決、凡事想拖的處置。從秦的時序看，這一役安排在滅楚之後並非偶然：南方大軍未及歸國，糧械仍在前線，再調重兵北上就必須先等楚地安定；所以先取荊南、降越，把整個南部邊界封住，才回師北上。燕廷對此心知肚明，拖延一日是一日，一旦秦軍騰出手來，遼東的深山也擋不住那種步步為營的進逼。
causeEn: The reason Yan could still be chased into Liaodong at all is that it came last in Qin's order of conquest. In 227 BC Qin sent Pang Huan against Yan, and Yan answered by sending Jing Ke to kill the king of Qin at Xianyang; when the attempt failed, Qin acquired a legitimate grievance to strike back. In 226 BC the Qin army entered Ji, King Xi handed over territory and sued for peace, and Qin took the land and set up commanderies, but King Xi did not truly submit to the north. He gathered a following in Liaodong and kept up dealings with the Rong and Di and with the Xiongnu. To King Zheng this was a thorn that had to be pulled out: Yan held the passes and roads of the north, and as long as it stood Qin could not safely commit troops and attention to the south and south-east. With Chu gone in 223 BC, only this one loose end remained in the north, and concentrating the army to close it out became the final step of the unification war. On the Yan side nothing new was attempted in 222 BC: there was no fresh attempt on the life of the king of Qin, and the war came entirely from Qin's intent to annex and from King Xi's habit of hesitating and letting things drag. The sequence matters: the campaign was placed after the fall of Chu for a reason. The southern army had not yet come home, its stores were still in the field, and to send a heavy force north Qin first had to wait for Chu to settle, so the lands south of the Jing were taken and Yue brought to terms to seal the southern frontier, and only then did the army turn north. The Yan court knew this: every day of delay was a day gained, and once the Qin army freed its hands, even the deep mountains of Liaodong could not hold off an advance made step by step.
impact: 這場追擊結束後，燕國這個自西周封建、立國八百餘年的北方政權從地圖上消失，它留下的並非戰國的封君版圖，而是秦的郡縣與後來漢的邊郡。燕地置郡之後，北方從漁陽、居庸到遼東、遼西連成一線，秦得以把官吏、刑名、度量衡與文字一路推到極北之地；前215年蒙恬率三十萬眾北逐匈奴、築長城與直道，所憑的就是這條此前斷續的北方防線。技術與物資層面上，遼東戰役推著秦的軍工再上一級：弩機零件標準化、鐵札甲成批生產、劍與戈按統一規格鑄造並刻銘，成為後世秦漢軍器工藝的骨架。對燕地而言，郡縣化意味著舊有封君秩序的徹底解體，貴族失去土地與部眾；之後兩千年的北方邊地經營，以遼東、遼西兩郡為起點，一路由中原延伸到草原。同一批秦軍在滅燕之後並未解散，而是就地改編為郡兵與戍卒，屯田與烽燧同時設置，遼水以北的遊牧部眾從此面對的是郡縣化的邊防，而不是諸侯的封境；秦漢之間八百年的北方拉鋸，邊界線的地形與據點大半沿用於此。兵器方面，戰國末年的刀劍冶鐵技術也在此時完成一次躍升，後來漢軍的常備裝備可以直接承接秦的規格。
impactEn: With the end of this pursuit the Yan state, which had been founded as a Western Zhou fief and had survived for more than eight centuries, disappeared from the map. What it left behind was not a Warring States principality but the Qin commanderies and the Han border commanderies that followed them. Once Yan was turned into commanderies, the north was joined into a single line from Yuyang and Juyong to Liaodong and Liaoxi, and Qin could carry its officials, its laws, its weights and measures and its script all the way to the far north; when Meng Tian took three hundred thousand men north in 215 BC to drive off the Xiongnu and to build the Great Wall and the direct road, he was relying on a northern defence line that had been broken and discontinuous until this campaign closed it. At the level of technique and supply, the Liaodong war pushed the Qin arsenals up a step: crossbow triggers were standardised, iron lamellar armour was produced in batches, and swords and ge were cast to a common pattern and inscribed, which became the skeleton of Qin and Han military craft. For the Yan lands, commandery government meant the complete dissolution of the old order of enfeoffed lords, and the nobles lost their lands and their retainers; the two thousand years of frontier administration that followed began with the two commanderies of Liaodong and Liaoxi and ran from the central plains out to the steppe. The same Qin army was not disbanded after the fall of Yan but converted on the spot into commandery troops and garrisons, with fields and beacon towers set up at once, so that the herders north of the Liao now faced a defended commandery frontier rather than the marches of a feudal lord. Most of the positions and the terrain of the eight hundred years of northern warfare between Qin and Han were inherited from that line. At the level of arms, the metallurgy of the late Warring States passed through a further step here, and the standard equipment of the later Han army could take over Qin's patterns directly.
result: 公元前222年，秦軍追入遼東，燕王喜走保遼東之後終於兵敗，傳世記載多說他死於遼東，廟號烈王；燕國的旗號自此收卷，燕地正式劃入秦的郡縣體系，成為九郡。與此同時，王翦、蒙武在南方略取荊南、降越君、置九郡，北方與南方的兩條戰線在同一年收束。前221年秦王政滅齊、稱皇帝、頒郡縣與度量衡文字之制，六國至此全部結束，同年蒙恬北擊匈奴的籌備亦已開始。就結果而言，這不是一場勢均力敵的對抗，而是一次兼併的收尾：秦軍靠的是前二百年間累積的冶鐵、徵發、糧道與郡縣行政能力；燕軍在失去都城與大將之後，靠著遼東的地形拖延了有限的一段時間，最後連這段時間也用完了。對燕國舊部而言，遼東的陷落意味著再無復國的可能：燕王喜既死，燕氏宗族分散降秦或北走塞外，數十年後仍有燕人起兵反秦，都已不成為建國的基底，只能是亂軍之號。對秦而言，此役的意義除了滅掉一個諸侯，更在於確認了郡縣兵制、冶鐵軍工與千里糧道能夠承載一次跨越半個燕地的遠征，而不必依靠臨時徵發的民力硬撐。
resultEn: In 222 BC the Qin army drove into Liaodong. King Xi of Yan took refuge there, was defeated, and the transmitted accounts say that he died in Liaodong; he is remembered as King Lie of Yan. The Yan banner was folded for the last time and the old lands were formally drawn into the commandery system of Qin as nine commanderies. At the same time, in the south, Wang Jian and Meng Wu took the lands south of the Jing, brought the king of Yue to terms and set up nine more commanderies, so the northern and southern lines of the campaign closed in the same year. In 221 BC Qin took Qi, assumed the title of emperor and promulgated the commandery system together with uniform weights, measures and script; the six states were finished, and the arrangements for Meng Tian's northern offensive against the Xiongnu were already under way. In result this was not a contest between evenly matched armies but the closing stage of an annexation. The Qin army drew on two centuries of accumulated ironworking, conscription, grain roads and commandery administration; the Yan army, having lost its capital and its generals, held out only as long as the terrain of Liaodong allowed, and then even that time ran out. For the old men of Yan, the fall of Liaodong meant there would be no restoration: with King Xi dead, the Yan clan scattered, some surrendering to Qin and some driven north beyond the frontier, and for decades afterwards Yan men still rose against Qin, but they had no basis on which to found a state again, only a name to raise a banner under. For Qin the meaning of the campaign reached further than the removal of one feudal lord. It confirmed that the commandery army, the iron foundries and the thousand-li grain road could carry a campaign across half the territory of Yan without having to lean on hastily conscripted peasants to do it.
